method: Sector score is the average 5-pillar composite of that sector's names in the Opportunities Book. Trend compares this week's average with last week's.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Best sector for a second straight week: CVX made a 52-week high at 214.06, COP and VLO near highs, Brent +8.7% on the week.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: JPM +0.76% and GS +0.92% as September hike odds reached 81-90% after core CPI came in at +0.3% m/m.

sectors.name: AI hardware & networking
sectors.note: The week's leadership: DELL +11.98% to a 52-week high, ANET +5.61%, VRT +3.60% on Oracle's ~$95bn capex reaffirmation.

sectors.name: Industrials & electrification
sectors.note: ETN +3.96% and GEV +3.61% on the data-centre power read-through; DE -0.32% and GE -0.15% drifted.

sectors.name: AI semis & compute
sectors.note: Mixed: AMD +2.49% and TSM +1.22% on Sep 11 but NVDA flat at -0.03% and MU -0.22% - the bid moved downstream to hardware.

sectors.name: Mega-cap platforms
sectors.note: GOOGL +1.77% led as Communication Services topped Friday's sector table; META +0.57% and MSFT +0.65% lagged.

sectors.name: Consumer & special situations
sectors.note: Split: FISV +5.42% on the new CEO's Sep 10 Goldman presentation, MELI -0.47% with no catalyst.

sectors.name: Software & security
sectors.note: Weakest group: PANW -2.32% on a +0.86% S&P day, NOW +1.04% but still 31.9% below its high with a hike likely Sep 16.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.note: Laggard again: UNH -2.37% and BSX -0.28% on a +0.86% S&P day; only ISRG +2.41% bounced, from near its 52-week low.

sectors.name: Power & nuclear
sectors.note: Decoupling from AI capex: CEG -0.43% and CCJ -0.76% on an up day, in the week UBS cut NuScale to Sell and SMR fell 15.67%.
